notes.app/services/director/h3_dialogue.py: Deferred: upstream churn in this file was 0 for 2.4.1, so it costs nothing today. Extraction is its own project; the budget keeps it from growing meanwhile.
notes.app/services/director_pipeline.py: Deferred for the same reason: upstream did not touch it in 2.4.1. Raised from 1808 by the two lines of the writer binding: the import, and the one value that now comes from the run rather than from the settings. A deliberate raise rather than an extraction, and the only one in this file: its extraction is the deferred project above, and the nearest removable lines are the PEP8 spacing between its functions or the comment explaining why a cleared beat cache lost a shot's dialogue -- both worse to lose than three lines of budget are to add.
New seam, and as small as a seam gets: the import of CoverControls and the one line that renders it. The panel itself is upstream's; the cover section, its reading call and its rules live in our own module, which owns no source of its own (the recording is audio_guide, the same parameter YuE2's picker writes).
notes.ui/src/components/LoraBrowser/InstalledC: New seam, eleven lines: a badge, a Remove button and the wrapper that lets the second one sit beside the card. This is the view that lists an imported checkpoint, so the two affordances have to render here, but both live in our own ImportedCheckpointHealth.tsx. Reported from use: deleting the weights by hand left the checkpoint listed as installed, with no rescan and no way to remove it, and the model list kept offering weights that were already gone.
notes.ui/src/api/client.ts: Priority: upstream edits this file (deleteOutput in 2.4.1), and our delete guard lives inside it. Raised from 15 by one line: the optional `missing` flag on InstalledCheckpoint, which upstream's own interface declares. The removal call lives in ui/src/api/importedCheckpoints.ts and the component imports it directly, so this file gains no new runtime import.
notes.ui/src/components/SettingsDrawer/Service: Priority: upstream edits this panel. Our lines are the Strata provider entry: the option, the address it is recognised by, the two lines that make it the remote transport with a URL filled in, and hiding LM Studio's memory control, whose native API Strata does not implement. The address check itself lives in ui/src/lib/strataProvider.ts, and the backend decides the behaviour, so a merge that takes upstream's panel keeps compiling and only loses the preset.
notes.ui/src/components/DirectorDashboard/Dire: Raised from 592 by two lines when the prompt audit became visible: the import of our PromptAuditNotices and the one line that renders it beside the planning log, so the findings are read before the render they describe is bought. The component, its fetch and its layout are ours; this file keeps the import and the render site. Both are deliberate raises and both are as small as the feature can be -- there is no once-per-pipeline host of ours in this view that the notices could ride inside, and no comment was left on them.

notes.app/launch.py: Priority: upstream edits it. Our lines are the Director slot guard and its endpoints, plus the imported-checkpoint seam: one import and one router include, one line in /checkpoints/installed that marks a registration whose weights are gone, and one in /models/reload that forgets a definition whose file vanished. notes.app/services/llm_service.py: Priority: upstream edits it. Lowered from 25 while adding the remote dialect: the idle-unload policy moved out to app/services/llm_idle.py, which paid for the three seams the dialect needed (the import, one call in _finalize_payload that both request paths already pass through, and letting the two grammar sites state the request instead of each deciding what to send). Every rule about which endpoint receives which form lives in app/services/llm_remote_dialect.py. Two more seams paid for the same way, by compressing the comments at the grammar sites: is_loaded now asks app/services/llm_writer_health.py whether a remote writer really answers, and the remote failure path asks it for the sentence that names the address to go and start.

notes.app/requirements.txt: One line that must survive: the setuptools pin, because ctranslate2 imports pkg_resources and without it every transcription is skipped.
notes.tests/test_gallery_active_media.py: New seam: one upstream test asserted the private shape of the height store (useState keyed by outputIds), which our identity-keyed useRef cannot satisfy. It is rewritten to pin the behaviour it names -- a measured height reflows the virtualized offsets at once -- so the regression is still caught without pinning either implementation.
notes..gitignore: One line, and the smallest seam here: app/writer_supervision.json is machine-specific (it holds the command that starts this machine's writer), so it must not be committed. Adding it to the ignore list is the only way to keep it out of the repository, and the line is a path, not code: a merge that takes upstream's side loses the ignore and shows the file as untracked, which is visible and harmless, unlike committing a local path. Raised from 1 to 2 for the same reason and the same kind of path: app/director_review_gate.json holds this machine's answer to 'stop after the shot images and wait for me', which is a preference rather than part of the project, and the alternative -- writing our setting into upstream's own config file -- would put a key upstream does not know about into a file it rewrites.
